archimate:Folder.name: 1 Business Roles and Actors
archimate:Folder.documentation:
The Business Roles and Actors component of the SAF describes the human and organizational dimension of the statistical enterprise — the people, groups, and external parties that perform activities, assume responsibilities, and interact within and across organizational boundaries. While processes and capabilities describe what and how the organization operates, roles and actors define who performs those operations and under what accountability structures.
In the SAF, a business role represents a defined responsibility or function assigned to one or more actors. It embodies the authority, duties, and expectations associated with a particular area of activity, independent of individual job titles or departmental hierarchies. For example, roles such as Data Steward, Statistician, Research Coordinator, or Process Owner can be consistently modeled and reused across processes, enabling standardized governance and accountability structures within the architecture.
A business actor is an individual, group, or external entity that enacts one or more roles. Actors may be internal (e.g., Methodology Department, Data Collection Division) or external (e.g., Partner Institution, Data Provider, Researcher). In the SAF, external actors are of particular importance, reflecting the growing interconnectedness of the statistical ecosystem, where collaboration with national, European, and international partners — as well as data providers and users — is central to value creation.
By explicitly defining business roles and actors, the SAF ensures that responsibilities are transparent and traceable throughout the organization’s processes and value streams. This modeling supports governance frameworks, role-based access control, and quality assurance mechanisms. It also facilitates the alignment of business architecture with organizational structures and human resource planning, enabling the design of adaptable and future-ready operating models.
Ultimately, the Business Roles & Actors view within the SAF emphasizes that the statistical system is not solely a technical or procedural construct — it is a collaborative enterprise built on the expertise, stewardship, and accountability of people and institutions working together to produce value for society.
